title: Gluten-Free Blueberry Almond Cupcakes
shortDescription: Gluten-free almond cupcakes with whole blueberries, ready in about 43 minutes including a swirled vanilla topping.
description: These gluten-free cupcakes use almond flour and a gluten-free blend to hold whole blueberries without sinking. The batter stays slightly thick on purpose, so the berries stay put through baking. I tested this batch three times in my home kitchen before the berries stopped sinking to the bottom. The trick is tossing them in a bit of the dry mix first. On top, a simple vanilla buttercream gets a light purple swirl using blueberry juice. It looks fancy but takes five extra minutes. These are great for spring brunches or anyone who needs a gluten-free treat that does not taste like a compromise.
ingredients: 1 1/4 cups gluten-free all-purpose flour blend (with xanthan gum)
1 cup fresh blueberries, plus 2 tbsp reserved dry mix for tossing
1 tbsp blueberry juice (mashed and strained from a few extra berries)
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a muffin tin with 12 paper liners.
Whisk gluten-free flour, almond flour, baking powder, and salt in a bowl. Set aside 2 tablespoons of this mix for tossing berries.
Beat softened butter and sugar until light, about 2 minutes. Add eggs one at a time, then vanilla and almond extract.
Add the flour mix and milk in three parts, alternating, starting and ending with flour. Batter should be thick, not runny.
Toss blueberries in the reserved dry mix. Fold them into the batter gently, keeping berries whole.
Divide batter evenly among liners, filling each about two thirds full. Bake 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool cupcakes in the tin for 5 minutes, then move to a wire rack to cool fully before frosting.
For frosting, beat butter until smooth. Add powdered sugar in two batches, beating well after each.
Spoon frosting into a piping bag. Drizzle a thin line of blueberry juice inside the bag along one side, then pipe a tall swirl on each cupcake for a natural marbled look.
tips: Toss the blueberries in dry mix before folding them in. This keeps them from sinking to the bottom.
Keep the batter thick. If it looks loose, add one more tablespoon of gluten-free flour before adding berries.
Use room temperature eggs and butter so the batter mixes smoothly without overworking the gluten-free flour.
Chill fresh blueberries for 10 minutes before folding in. Cold berries hold their shape better in the oven.

faq.question: Why do my blueberries sink to the bottom of gluten-free cupcakes?
faq.answer: Sinking happens when the batter is too thin to hold the berries in place. Keep this batter thick and toss berries in flour first to help them stay suspended.

faq.question: Can I use frozen blueberries instead of fresh?
faq.answer: Yes, but do not thaw them first. Toss frozen berries straight from the freezer in the reserved dry mix, then fold in quickly so they do not bleed color into the batter.

faq.question: What gluten-free flour blend works best for this recipe?
faq.answer: Use a 1:1 gluten-free baking blend that already includes xanthan gum. Blends without xanthan gum can make the crumb too crumbly for whole berries.

faq.question: How do I get the vanilla swirl to look marbled instead of solid purple?
faq.answer: Add the blueberry juice in one thin line inside the piping bag, not mixed into the frosting. This creates a natural swirl pattern as you pipe.

conclusion: These cupcakes prove gluten-free baking can still hold whole fruit and look bakery-pretty on top. Give the thick batter a try and let the berries do the work.
